summary: Susanne Hoeber Rudolph (1930–2015) was an Indology scholar who earned degrees from Sarah Lawrence College, Harvard University, and Radcliffe College. She taught political science at Harvard (~1955–1963) and became a professor at the University of Chicago in 1964.

Susanne Mrozik is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She earned an M.T.S. at Harvard University, studying under Diana L. Eck, Charles Hallisey, Stephanie W. Jamison, and Margaret R. Miles. She held posts at Western Michigan University and Mount Holyoke College.

Sushanta Sen is a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Visva-Bharati University, he served there as a lecturer in 1986 and was a lecturer in Indian religions in the Department of Theology at the University of Birmingham.

Sushil Kumar De (1890–1968) was an Indology scholar educated at Presidency College, Calcutta University, SOAS, and the University of Bonn. He taught English at Calcutta and Presidency College, served as Professor of Sanskrit at Dhaka (~1923–1947), and led Jadavpur's Bengali department.

Susumu Kajiura (born 1957) is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He held a post at Kyoto University in 1999 and served as head of humanities research at the Gangoji Institute for Research on Cultural Property (attested 2001).

Susumu Otake (born 1974) is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at the University of Tsukuba (~1993–2002) under Makio Takemura. He later held part-time lecturer posts at Kyoto University, Bukkyo University, and Hanazono University.

Susumu Shimazono (born 1948) is a religious studies and Japanology scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley. He was Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tokyo (1995–2013) and later held posts at Sophia University.

Susumu Yamaguchi (1895–1976) was an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Sylvain Lévi and Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He served as a professor at Otani University (1934–1964).

Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri (born 1936) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the universities of London, Pennsylvania, and Toronto. He founded and served as president of Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies and held posts at Toronto and Ontario Tech University.

Suzanne Karpelès (1890–1968) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Louis Finot. She held posts at the EFEO, National Library of Cambodia, and the Buddhist Institute.

Suzanne Newcombe is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed a doctorate at the University of Cambridge. She has held posts at Cambridge, the London School of Economics, Inform, King's College London, and the Open University.

Sven Hedin (1865–1952) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his studies at the University of Stockholm, Uppsala University, the University of Berlin, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg.
Sven Wittemann is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

Swami Dayananda Saraswati (1930–2015) was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Bangalore Sanskrit College and trained under Chinmayananda Saraswati, P. S. Subramania Iyer, Swami Tapovan Maharaj, Swami Pranavananda, and Swami Tarananda Giri.
Swami Lakshman Joo (1907–1991) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Maheshwar Nath Razdan from 1926 to 1933 and founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship in 1991.

Swami Maheshanandagiri Maharaj is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served as Mahamandaleshvar Pontiff at Dakshinamurti Peetha (attested 1980) and founded the Mahesh Research Institute and Advaita Grantha Ratna Manjusha.
Swami Satyananda Puri (1902–1942) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta and also held an academic post there.

Swami Sivananda Saraswati (1887–1963) was a religious studies, philosophy, and Indology figure who studied at Thanjavur Medical College (~1903–1907). He founded the Divine Life Society in 1936 and the Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy in 1948.
Swami Vimalananda (1872–1908) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Ripon College and became a disciple of Swami Vivekananda in 1897.

Swami Vivekananda (1863–1902) was a philosopher and Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Presidency University, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta (~1879–1884), and was a disciple of Ramakrishna (~1881–1886).
